reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it actively promotes OneCoin as a wealth-building opportunity, urging viewers to purchase packages, mine coins, recruit others and act quickly while emphasizing substantial commissions and appreciation. The presentation describes a binary right-and-left sales-team structure with tier-dependent bonuses, while presenting paid educational packages and mining access as routes to profit. Its repeated wealth claims, recruitment instructions and urgency make the main communicative action solicitation rather than neutral cryptocurrency education.

citations.quote: Then we have a network bonus. We do use a binary compensation plan.
you get 4 levels of matching bonuses 10%, 10%, 20%, and 25%
So, to get into mining, you've got to have some form of tokens. We give out tokens to you with your educational packages and that gives you the ability to go mine coins.
We are selling educational packages, folks. We're not selling coins, okay? We're not selling investments.
we do have a split coming up probably five or eight days and that will give you the opportunity to double your tokens

opening.argument: Judge the financial claims by their qualifications, not just their enthusiasm. The speaker describes resale in terms of what buyers are willing to pay, not a guaranteed return. He also poses the possibility of no buyers. Even the projected market position is framed conditionally, with uncertainty about the price required. Those qualifications matter: the presentation makes a bullish case for digital currency, but its own account leaves future demand and resale value unresolved.

citations.quote: And whatever people are willing to pay for them, you can sell them for that price.
Now if there's no buyers Well the
as our coin grows in value to over, say say, I don't know, $7, will probably be larger than Bitcoin

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited compensation terms show how the speaker says the plan works; they do not establish that returns are guaranteed. The mining passage likewise describes access through packages, while the speaker expressly characterizes what is sold as education rather than an investment. The proposed token split is time-sensitive, but urgency alone does not settle whether a financial presentation is deceptive.

citations.quote: We are selling educational packages, folks. We're not selling coins, okay? We're not selling investments.
we do have a split coming up probably five or eight days and that will give you the opportunity to double your tokens

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Conditional resale language does not change the pitch's central action. Viewers are told to purchase a package, become miners and share the story with friends and family. The presentation also connects sales-team structure to bonuses and presses viewers to decide quickly to obtain more tokens. Those are concrete recruitment and purchase prompts, not merely a forecast with risk qualifications.

citations.quote: Purchase a OneCoin digital education package, become a OneCoin miner, set up the OneCoin marketing system, and then share the OneCoin story with your friends and family.
Then we have a network bonus. We do use a binary compensation plan.
if you're looking to make a decision you need to make one ASAP

opening.argument: This is presented as instruction in an unfamiliar technology. The speaker calls the format a 'present training,' says he hopes to define unfamiliar terms, and describes courses, a wallet, trading, mining and a blockchain view in the back office. That scope gives the judge a reason to read the compensation discussion as one part of a broader operational walkthrough. A presentation can describe how participants might earn money without every explanatory passage becoming a deceptive solicitation.

citations.quote: I call this a present training
there's a lot of words that you may not know and hopefully i'll be able to define those for you tonight
We got a whole bunch of courses back there A very comprehensive trading program.
you can do trading, you can do mining, you can look at the blockchain

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's quotations identify a bonus structure and token-enabled mining, but those excerpts alone do not erase the instructional material surrounding them. The speaker says viewers can set up a free account to inspect the back office, and asks purchasers to pass the courses and start learning. A walkthrough that includes commercial terms can still have a substantial educational purpose.

citations.quote: you can set up an account for free. You can go and check out the whole back office. Learn all you want.
we want you to pass all of your courses we want you to start learning

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling the presentation training does not make its purpose neutral. The speaker explicitly says the training should lead viewers to decide to dig in, then gives a sequence beginning with purchasing a package and ending with sharing the story. The paid packages provide mining tokens, and selling packages earns a direct sales bonus. The instructional elements serve that purchase-and-recruitment pitch.

citations.quote: we want you to see so much information that you go wow this is something I really ought to dig in tonight
Purchase a OneCoin digital education package, become a OneCoin miner, set up the OneCoin marketing system, and then share the OneCoin story with your friends and family.
We give out tokens to you with your educational packages and that gives you the ability to go mine coins.
when you go out and sell one of our educational packages he did a ten percent direct sales bonus

opening.argument: The described transaction has an identifiable product and an identifiable sales commission: educational packages, including a free entry option, with a stated direct-sales bonus when a package is sold. The speaker also describes courses and a trading program. A commission schedule does not by itself show that customers receive nothing or that the educational service is fictitious. The judge should distinguish a disclosed, if aggressive, package-and-referral business pitch from proof of a deceptive scheme.

citations.quote: We are selling educational packages, folks. We're not selling coins, okay? We're not selling investments.
you can set up an account for free. You can go and check out the whole back office.
when you go out and sell one of our educational packages he did a ten percent direct sales bonus
We got a whole bunch of courses back there A very comprehensive trading program.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The right-and-left teams and matching percentages establish a tiered compensation plan, but do not alone establish that the courses are nonexistent or that anyone is promised a guaranteed payout. The prosecution also cites a coming token split; that is a promotional incentive, but the cited line does not demonstrate an actual return. Those distinctions matter when evaluating what this presentation itself proves.

citations.quote: We do use a binary compensation plan. So if you're familiar with binaries, you have a right sales team and a left sales team.
you get 4 levels of matching bonuses 10%, 10%, 20%, and 25%
we do have a split coming up probably five or eight days and that will give you the opportunity to double your tokens

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The issue is the mechanism being promoted, not whether a course page exists. Packages supply tokens for mining; package sales pay commissions; and higher entry levels unlock matching bonuses. The speaker also says qualifying for binary income requires a trader package on each side. That ties payment, recruiting and income eligibility together despite the educational-product framing.
